source.statement: Decision CORE-015-SCROLL-THRESHOLD-2026-11-20 approves the scroll alignment confidence threshold 0.95 with its 15% ambiguity margin: a join is accepted only when at least 95% of the informative overlap rows agree at the best offset and the best offset beats its runner-up by the margin; repeating content scales confidence down instead of guessing and thin overlaps below 8 informative rows carry no evidence. The two leading references converge on a 5%-difference budget for row-level identity - ShareX's scrolling combiner demands unbroken byte-identical row runs (ScrollingCaptureManager.CombineImages), and long-shot-rs treats rows as identical when at most 5% of pixels differ (src/stitch.rs width/20) - so 0.95 keeps CORE-015's no-seamless-claim promise on the conservative side of both. The join decision is refactored into one production seam (xerahs::capture::scrollJoinDecision) shared by the stitcher, the conformance adapter and eight new CORE-015 scroll-join-disposition vectors in CORE-PLATFORM-001/test-vectors.json (39/39 pass through the Linux adapter; the same dispositions are asserted natively). The threshold value the placeholder held is approved unchanged, so no runtime behavior changes. The other fifteen packages carry forward to contract 0.4.2 unchanged in normative text from 0.4.1, where the 2026-11-19 EO-004 record approved them; the deciding agent verified that carry-forward by inspecting this commit's diff, which touches no other capability package. No ROOT constitution rule is changed.
